questions.q: According to the summary, what must you do to make money from your passion?
a: Turn yourself into a brand
Build a physical store
Hire a marketing agency
Wait for the right moment
questions.why: Lesson 1 says you can profit by being yourself, but only once you have built a public brand.

questions.q: What did Gary do to establish his own brand?
a: Talked about wine in everyday terms across many YouTube episodes
Wrote a newspaper column about the restaurant industry
Ran television ads for his family's wine business
Hosted a weekly radio show about marketing
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes his 1,000 YouTube episodes about wine as the start of his brand.

questions.q: How should you choose which online platform to use?
a: Pick one that matches your personality and strengths
Choose whichever platform has the most users that year
Use every platform equally, no matter your style
Start with the platform your competitors use most
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends matching the medium to who you are, such as video for extroverts or blogs for long-winded writers.

questions.q: What example shows a mismatch between a person and a platform?
a: A long-winded writer struggling to fit ideas into short tweets
An introvert posting long essays on a blogging site
A photographer sharing images on a photo app
A speaker publishing recordings of talks as a podcast
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses the author's own difficulty with Twitter's character limit as the example.

questions.q: What does the summary say about being authentic and losing some followers?
a: You will lose people either way, so keep being yourself
You should tone down your personality to keep everyone
You should copy whoever is most popular on the platform
You should hide your real interests until you are famous
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that authenticity always turns some people off, so it is better to lose those who would not like the real you.
